n: A song of Zion: the Lord is great and deserves great praise in Jerusalem, his holy mountain. The city is honored because God dwells there.

f.g: Mount Zion, the temple hill in Jerusalem.

n: Mount Zion is beautiful in its height and a joy to the whole earth. “The sides of the north” borrows a phrase for the sacred mountain where God was said to dwell.

f.g: Beautiful in its elevation — lovely and lofty.
Hebrew Zaphon — a name for the holy mountain of the gods in Canaanite lore, here claimed for the true God.

f.w: the city of the great King

n: God himself, not the city’s walls, is its true fortress.
Enemy kings joined forces and advanced together against the city.
But when they saw it, they were stunned, panicked, and fled. Some connect this with the sudden collapse of the Assyrian siege in Hezekiah’s day.
Terror gripped them like the pains of a woman in labor — sudden and unstoppable.
God shatters even the great ocean-going ships with an east wind. Their power is nothing before him.

f.g: Large merchant ships built for long voyages — a symbol of human pride and wealth.
A hot, violent wind from the desert.

n: What our ancestors told us, we have now seen for ourselves: God protects his city forever. Testimony moves from hearing to seeing.

f.w: As we have heard, so have we seen

n: Inside the temple, the worshippers reflect on God’s loyal love.

f.g: Meditated on, pictured in our minds.

n: God’s praise spreads as far as his fame — to the ends of the earth — and his right hand acts with justice.

f.g: As widely as your reputation reaches.

n: Let Zion and the towns of Judah celebrate God’s just decisions.

f.g: The towns and villages of Judah, or its women.

n: An invitation to walk around the city and count its towers — to see for yourself how safe it is.
Study its defenses and palaces so you can describe them to your children. Faith is meant to be passed on.

f.w: tell it to the generation following

n: The real point: Zion’s true defense is God himself, who will lead us always — even through death.

f.g: Some manuscripts read “forever”; either way, God guides his people to the end.
